title: fix(jdbc): preserve detected frameworks on client info updates

files.patch:
@@ -101,7 +101,7 @@ Compatibility-sensitive traits:
 - Geometry type mapping: For ClickHouse `25.11+`, where `Geometry` changed from a string alias to `Variant(Point, Ring, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon)`, JDBC exposes `Geometry` as `ARRAY`, returns nested Java arrays from `getObject()`/`getArray()`, and accepts `Struct` or nested `Array` inputs for prepared-statement inserts depending on the geometry shape. For ClickHouse `26.8+` the variant also carries `MultiPoint`.
 - MultiPoint type mapping: For ClickHouse `26.8+`, JDBC exposes `MultiPoint` as `ARRAY` with type name `MultiPoint`, returns `double[][]` from `getObject()` and a `java.sql.Array` from `getArray()`, and accepts a nested `Array` (`createArrayOf("Array(Point)", ...)`) for prepared-statement inserts, the same as `Ring` and `LineString`.
 - IP address type mapping: JDBC exposes `IPv4` and `IPv6` as `OTHER`. `getObject()` returns a `java.net.Inet4Address` for `IPv4` and a `java.net.InetAddress` for `IPv6` (an `Inet6Address`, or an `Inet4Address` for an IPv4-mapped value such as `::ffff:10.0.0.1`). `ResultSetMetaData#getColumnClassName` reports `java.net.Inet4Address` and `java.net.InetAddress` respectively, also for the `VALUE` column of `java.sql.Array#getResultSet()`, and `java.sql.Array#getArray()` returns an `Inet4Address[]` or an `InetAddress[]`.
-- Client info propagation: Supports JDBC client info such as `ApplicationName` and forwards it to the underlying client name. The `client_id_metadata` connection property is forwarded to the client and adds key/value pairs to the `User-Agent` header (see the `client-v2` `User-Agent` entry).
+- Client info propagation: Supports JDBC client info such as `ApplicationName` and forwards it to the underlying client name. Detected frameworks (for example Apache Spark) are added to the `User-Agent` comment group as a `fw` entry (`fw:apache.spark`), unless framework detection is disabled or `client_id_metadata` sets `fw`; updating or clearing `ApplicationName` keeps them. The `client_id_metadata` connection property is forwarded to the client and adds key/value pairs to the `User-Agent` header (see the `client-v2` `User-Agent` entry).
 - Wrapper support: Implements standard JDBC `Wrapper` and `unwrap` behavior on major JDBC objects.
 - Packaging and runtime compatibility: Ships as a JDBC 4.2 driver, depends on `client-v2`, and includes native-image metadata for GraalVM users.

@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+- **[jdbc-v2]** Keep detected frameworks in the `User-Agent` header after
+  `Connection.setClientInfo("ApplicationName", ...)`. The driver now sends them as an `fw` entry in the comment group
+  (`... jdbc-v2/<version> clickhouse-java-v2/<version> (fw:apache.spark; lv:...)`) instead of a second
+  parenthesized group after the client name. Null and empty application names
+  remove only the application prefix, without adding leading whitespace. Empty `client_name` and legacy `product_name`
+  values also no longer add leading whitespace when connecting.
+  (https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-java/issues/3219)
